scope: Explicit cross-book comparisons; unseen or unmatched document-division signs are not assigned.

new_designs.name: Percent sign, narrow italic
new_designs.identity_reason: The complete eight-point impression is visibly narrower than every reviewed Boston italic percent counterpart; the ten-point GPO impression repeats its construction with weaker ink. Threshold 230 follows the observed faint slash and closes both printed oval counters. The threshold 225 trial left the upper counter open and was rejected; no missing connection is drawn by hand. No diagonal is redrawn.

new_designs.name: Scruple, open arc and detached centre bar
new_designs.identity_reason: The eight- and ten-point GPO settings share a plain-ended open arc with a short detached central wedge/bar. The matching document-division ten-point impression independently repeats both features. All reviewed Boston scruples have inward end serifs and a connected centre bar. The selected larger GPO impression is complete.

document_witnesses.reason: Independent construction/proportion evidence; the selected jobroom impression has sharper native ink.

new_designs.name: Equality sign, widely separated strokes
new_designs.identity_reason: The two twelve-point GPO impressions have centre separation about0.37of stroke length, wider than the reviewed Boston settings. The document-division twelve-point row independently repeats the wide separation. The cleaner algebraic impression avoids paper flecks between the repeated mathematical impression.

new_designs.name: Greater-than sign, broad angle

new_designs.name: Plus-minus sign, detached lower bar
new_designs.identity_reason: The legend shows a complete upright cross separated from the lower bar by a clear gap persisting throughout the threshold comparison. All seven Boston plus-minus forms have an attached descending stem. The document-division eight-point row also prints a separated lower bar, but its broader proportions are recorded as related evidence rather than an exact counterpart.
